comparison: Both evaluate ch1-4 mutant claims (C12-C27) but reach different conclusions. OpenEval finds the evidence well-supported across multiple experimental approaches. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, raising concerns about growth conditions (short day vs long day, light intensity, temperature effects) and requesting clarification on mutant nomenclature. OpenEval also includes abstract claims C1-C3 which peer reviewers address separately.

Both evaluate sugar treatment claims (C31-C42) with divergent assessments. OpenEval finds the evidence strongly supported, praising the use of metabolically inactive sugar controls and mechanistic insights. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, identifying major inconsistencies with related studies regarding cycloheximide effects and questioning the rationale for using different sugar concentrations across experiments (0.5-20 mM vs ~50 mM).

Both evaluate MIR156A/C mutant claims (C43-C57) and agree the evidence is supported. OpenEval praises the comprehensive genetic and molecular characterization. Peer reviewers did not raise specific concerns about these findings, accepting the genetic evidence for MIR156A/C as dominant regulators.

Both evaluate sugar regulation of MIR156A/C expression (C58-C67) but differ in assessment. OpenEval finds claims supported while acknowledging mechanistic uncertainty. Peer reviewers express greater uncertainty, identifying major inconsistencies with other studies regarding transcriptional vs post-transcriptional regulation, requesting experiments under common conditions, and asking for quantification of GUS activity.

Both evaluate HXK1 signaling claims (C68-C79, with peer review also including C5) but reach different conclusions. OpenEval finds the evidence well-supported, praising the catalytically inactive mutant control. Peer reviewers express substantial uncertainty, questioning growth conditions (16°C vs 22°C, 60 vs 200 μmol light), noting temperature effects on MIR156A, and requesting information on biological replicates and statistical significance.

Both evaluate defoliation experiments (C6, C80-C82) and find evidence supported. OpenEval notes the claims are appropriately supported while acknowledging some overstatement in claiming glucose is THE leaf factor. Peer reviewers did not raise specific concerns about this experimental approach, accepting the results as part of the overall advance.

Both evaluate high-level conclusions about sugar as an age signal (C4, C7, with OpenEval also covering C1-C3, C5). OpenEval finds abstract claims well-supported by comprehensive evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly state the finding is 'a significant advance' and accept the main conclusion despite noting the lack of endogenous sugar measurements, which they consider beyond scope.

OpenEval evaluates structural characterization claims (C121-C123) regarding RACE data for MIR156 genes and finds them supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific structural claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims about MIR156 family member expression patterns (C118-C120) using qRT-PCR in se-1 background and finds them supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific expression profiling claims.

OpenEval evaluates speculative mechanistic hypotheses (C124-C128) about differential sugar sensing and finds them appropriately uncertain, noting they are Discussion section speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific speculative claims.

OpenEval evaluates additional speculative hypotheses (C129-C135) about photoperiod, environmental factors, and broader implications, finding them appropriately uncertain as Discussion speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates background/literature claims (C8-C11, C86-C117) that establish context from prior work, finding them appropriately supported as cited literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are not novel findings but rather established background.
